questions.question: What is groundwater?
choices: Only water flowing in surface rivers
Water that exists only in caves
Water within connected pores and fractures below the water table
Water stored only inside living organisms

questions.question: What is the water table?
choices: The upper surface of the saturated groundwater zone
The bottom of every lake
The boundary between ocean water and ice
The surface of a rain cloud

questions.question: What is an aquifer?
choices: A rock unit that stores water but cannot transmit useful amounts
A geologic unit that stores and transmits usable amounts of groundwater
Only a large underground open cavern
Any dry layer above the water table

questions.question: What is groundwater recharge?
choices: The removal of groundwater by pumping
The flow of groundwater out through a spring
The replenishment of groundwater by water entering an aquifer
The evaporation of water directly from a stream

questions.question: What is permeability?
choices: The fraction of a rock's volume made of pores alone
How readily a material allows fluid to flow through connected spaces
The total mass of water above a rock layer
The rate of evaporation from a surface

questions.question: What is base flow in a stream?
choices: Only rapid surface runoff during a storm
Only water evaporating from the stream
The uphill movement of water toward a drainage divide
Flow supported by groundwater discharge between storms

questions.question: What is a drainage divide?
choices: Higher terrain separating neighboring drainage basins
A point where two tributaries join
The lowest point in one drainage basin
The upper boundary of saturated groundwater

questions.question: Why can pumping groundwater faster than recharge create problems?
choices: Stored groundwater and local water levels can decline
An aquifer always refills as quickly as it is pumped
Groundwater storage cannot change with withdrawal
Recharge necessarily increases enough to match pumping

questions.question: Why can pavement increase surface runoff?
choices: It always adds connected pore space to the ground
It makes all precipitation enter the aquifer directly
It often reduces infiltration into the ground
It reduces streamflow after every storm

questions.question: Why is porous rock not necessarily highly permeable?
choices: Porosity and permeability always measure the same property
Pores may be poorly connected
Every porous rock allows equally rapid flow
Only pore volume matters, not connections between pores

questions.question: How can pollution at the ground surface affect groundwater?
choices: Soil removes every contaminant completely
Groundwater never connects with surface infiltration
Only contaminants visible to the eye can move downward
Contaminants can move downward with infiltrating water

questions.question: Why do activities upstream matter to people downstream?
choices: Only rainfall at the river mouth influences downstream water
Flowing water can carry sediment and pollutants through the watershed
River flow prevents contaminants from traveling
Upstream and downstream sections never exchange water

questions.question: What can happen to a well when the water table falls below its intake?
choices: The well may no longer supply water
The well automatically deepens to meet the new water table
The pump creates enough new water to restore the table
All groundwater above the intake becomes surface runoff

questions.question: How can wetlands influence water moving through a watershed?
choices: They prevent every flood regardless of rainfall
They remove every dissolved contaminant completely
They can store water and slow its release
They always speed all runoff directly to the outlet

questions.question: Why are recharge areas important for groundwater protection?
choices: Recharge areas prevent water from reaching aquifers
Recharge areas are always the deepest part of an aquifer
Only pumping locations affect groundwater quality
Water entering there can replenish an aquifer and carry contaminants

questions.question: Two materials have similar porosity, but one has connected pores. Which should transmit groundwater more readily?
choices: The material with connected pores
The material with disconnected pores
Both must transmit no water
The darker material regardless of pore connections

questions.question: A watershed loses vegetation and gains extensive pavement. What change is generally expected after a storm?
choices: All infiltration necessarily increases
Streams receive no stormwater at all
The watershed's topographic divides disappear
More rapid surface runoff

questions.question: An aquifer receives 100 units of recharge and loses 140 units through pumping and other discharge. What is its storage change?
choices: An increase of 40 units
A decrease of 40 units
An increase of 240 units
No change

questions.question: A contaminant enters a tributary above a river's drinking-water intake. What should monitoring consider?
choices: Tributaries never connect to larger rivers
Flow guarantees instant removal of contaminants
The contaminant may move downstream toward the intake
Only water temperature can change downstream

questions.question: A map shows ridges around streams flowing to one lake. What do those ridges help identify?
choices: The exact age of the lake
The chemical formula of groundwater
The number of fish in the lake
The lake's watershed boundary
